method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/macro/citation comparison and reverse paraphrase with checked terminology; not independent or human review.
scope: All four translated blocks in Hilbert's Hotel, including the historical quotation and Dedekind-infinite definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Without presupposing the natural numbers, the text seeks a characterization of infinite sets. Hilbert contrasts a full finite hotel, where rearrangement frees no room, with a full hotel having rooms 1, 2, 3, and so on, where shifting every guest up by one frees room 1.
samples.checks: The 1924 date, quotation brackets, finite/infinite contrast, one-guest capacity, all room numbers, diagram commands, citation page and translation attribution are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The room-shift motivates Dedekind's 1888 definition: A is Dedekind infinite exactly when it injects into a proper subset of itself, equivalently when an injective self-map omits some element o.
samples.checks: The anachronism qualification, citation year, biconditional force, both injection markers, proper-subset relation, quantified element and range exclusion are unchanged.

source_observations.finding: The English modal phrase is grammatically malformed (‘must be characterize’).
source_observations.resolution: The Marathi expresses the unambiguous intended requirement directly and leaves the frozen source untouched.

limitations: No independent linguistic or historical review has been performed.
